sentences.text: This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C./483 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 266/2024. registered at Police Station, Nalchha District Dhar (M.P.) for offence punishable under Section (s) 366, 376(2), 506 of IPC.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 10.7.2024.
As per the case of prosecution, prosecutrix aged around 23 years, a married lady, submitted a written complaint to SHO P.S. Nalchha Dhar on 30.6.2024 that on 7.5.2023 she was alone at home.
Ramkishan s/o Munna came to her house and proposed to marry her.
She refused but Ramkishan threatened to kill her and took her to Rau Indore.
Ramkishan kept her in a rented room as his wife.
Ramkishan had physical relations with her on multiple occasions, but refused to marry her.
She stayed with Ramkishan for almost one year.
On 3.5.2024, when Ramkishan had gone out for labour NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:31943 2 MCRC-47979-2024 work, she returned to her paternal home at village Sebrimal.
She could not report due to fear of social disrepute.
She was married by her family members on 30.5.2024.
After her marriage, she informed her husband about the incident.
Ramkishan was abusing her husband on phone, therefore, she came to report with her husband.
On such allegations P.S. Nalchha District Dhar registered FIR at crime No.266 of 2024 for offence punishable under Sections 366, 376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC against the applicant.

sentences.text: Her statement were recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C.
In her statement recorded under section 164, she alleged rape against relatives of Ramkishan.
She alleged that Ramkishan, his father Munna, uncle Kakadiya, Chopadiya and friend Deepak had committed gang rape on her, while she was in confinement.
Ramkishan has threatened to disrepute by making her photos and videos viral.
Applicant was arrested on 10.7.2024.
He is in custody ever since.
On completion of investigation, final report has been submitted.
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the matter.
The inordinate delay in registration of FIR creates doubt in veracity of prosecution.
It was a case of consensual relationship.
Victim had left the applicant and married to some other person.
Almost after one month of marriage, false allegations are levelled against the applicant.
No offence as alleged is committed by applicant.
The applicant is aged around 25 years.
He is labourer by profession.
There is no likelihood of absconsion leaving his family, home and profession.

There is no likelihood NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:31943 3 MCRC-47979-2024 of tampering with evidence by the applicant.
The trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of the alleged offence and cites criminal history of one case against the applicant.
In reply, learned counsel for the applicant submits that the other matter is pending for trial.
He has never been convicted for any major offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
